newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus abandons fixed rouble policy.
newsitem.headline: Belarus abandons fixed rouble policy.

text.p: Belarus introduced a market rouble/dollar rate policy on Thursday to stimulate exports, replacing a fixed-rate regime, a government document published in local papers said.
The National Bank will now set a daily rate based on supply and demand at the Minsk Interbank Currency Exchange, adjusted for inflation, it said.
Commercial and interbank rates may not deviate from this rate by more than 1.5 percent, while the amount of brokers' commissions must not be over one percent.

National Bank currency regulation department head Sergei Gaiko told Reuters that only strategic importers will have the right to buy Russian roubles and dollars and 50 percent of currency earnings must be sold on the market as before.
In February the Belarus government introduced a fixed rate of 22,050 Belarussian roubles per dollar.

President Alexander Lukashenko keeps a tight grip on banks and prices. Economic reforms in Belarus are running at a much slower pace than in many other former Soviet republics, prompting international lending agencies to cut off funds.
But there have been signs of a thaw in relations with the International Monetary Fund and World Bank this year.
Gaiko said the new policy would help liberalise the economy and not lead to a crash of the rouble.
"This instruction is very important because the government will no longer be involved in the problem of setting the rate," he said. "It is the first step towards liberalising the currency market."
The real rouble rate was already set in Russia and Ukraine, he said, forecasting the rouble would gradually slip to about 27,000-31,000 per dollar.
On Thursday the rouble fell to 22,530 per dollar from 22,450 on Wednesday.
On the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange 10 Belarus roubles cost 1,972 Russian roubles, while banks in Moscow were quoting the Belarussian rouble at about 29,500 per dollar.
